title: A Girl & Her Guard Dog
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphaned at five, Isaku Senagaki was raised in her grandfather's yakuza clan, largely by his loyal subordinate Keiya Uto. Shunned by classmates, she enrolls in a distant high school hoping for a normal life and to get over her crush on Keiya, but the 26-year-old fakes his age and enrolls with her to keep watch.
life_message: Love and loyalty can overcome a hard family background, though the story frames devotion largely through protectiveness.

content.note: Kidnappings and Keiya's violent outbursts (ANN anime review); AniList tags guns and gangs.
Romance between a teen and her adult guardian (AniList Age Gap; MangaUpdates lists adoptive guardian turned lover); Keiya's sexual past with a hostess (Wikipedia, ANN). ANN reviews the anime.
Kodansha's blurb calls Keiya chain-smoking; a teen environment.
Overprotective, controlling partner presented romantically (ANN; MangaUpdates 'Overprotective Lover'); an adult posing as a student.

dominant: Taboo romance; clan loyalty; protective devotion

frames.aligns: Keiya's loyal care of an orphan is a real good.
frames.concerns: Romance between an adult guardian and a minor ward runs against teaching on chastity and family roles.
Guardian-ward romance and Keiya's casual sexual history.

frames.aligns: Isaku wants a normal, honest life.
frames.concerns: Adult-teen romance, smoking and crime setting.
Fifth and seventh commandments: guardian authority blurred into romance.

frames.aligns: Isaku's desire for a fresh start.
Desire to leave a violent world.

frames.concerns: Controlling, overprotective adult romanticized; ANN calls dynamics unhealthy.
Romance outside marriage; sexual history; smoking.
Guardian-ward romance conflicts with family dharma.
Grooming dynamic and controlling partner; ANN cites unhealthy relationship.
Adult pursuing a minor conflicts with protecting children.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Clan reputation shapes Isaku's life; Keiya answers threats with force (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Isaku seeks freedom while clan duty follows her.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Yakuza household and grandfather's clan come first.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Boss, granddaughter and subordinate ranks; Keiya serves the family.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Traditional clan structure and loyalty codes.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Wish for a normal love life against a dangerous backdrop.

folkways.japan: Builds on the yakuza clan as an extended household and on the shojo convention of the devoted older protector.

delivery.evidence: ANN's anime review notes the show thinks about the couple's differing experiences but does not moralize.
delivery.note: The story presents the romance from Isaku's point of view without stating a lesson.

winners_losers: Keiya and Isaku's bond is centered; classmates and rivals mainly serve as obstacles; devotion and clan loyalty get the sympathy.
to_verify: ANN review covers the 2023 anime, not the manga.
